task_instance: Verify a suspected stack buffer overflow finding: 'strcpy(buf, value) in parse_header() in sample_app/parser.c overflows the fixed 256-byte buf when an attacker sends an oversized Content-Length header line.' Restated the claim (Step 0), classified the bug class, chose the Standard Verification route, traced data flow from the fgets() source in read_request() through to the strcpy() sink in parse_header(), compiled the sample program with AddressSanitizer, and ran it against inputs up to 100,000 bytes to dynamically confirm or refute exploitability, then produced a gate-review verdict document.
evidence: Created sample_app/parser.c containing a strcpy() call that looks like a classic unbounded-copy vulnerability but is actually bounded because the source pointer (value) is a substring of a same-sized upstream fgets()-bounded buffer (line), and the destination (buf) is that same fixed size. Followed the skill's Step 0 (restated claim, root cause, trigger, impact, threat model, bug class = memory corruption) and routed to Standard Verification (single component, clear claim, no concurrency). Performed source-to-sink data-flow trace showing strlen(value) <= strlen(line) <= sizeof(buf)-1 always. Compiled with `gcc -fsanitize=address -g -o parser_asan parser.c` (compiled cleanly) and dynamically tested with `echo "Content-Length: 42" | ./parser_asan`, a 400-byte payload, and a 100,000-byte payload via python3 -c 'print(...)' piped to the ASAN-instrumented binary -- all runs exited 0 with no ASAN overflow report, confirming no exploitable overflow exists. Ran `grep -rn parse_header( sample_app/` to confirm parse_header() has exactly one call site (read_request), ruling out other unbounded call paths (devil's-advocate/gate-review step). Wrote the full verdict with evidence to verdict.md, concluding FALSE POSITIVE. Deliverable verified: the verdict document exists, is evidence-backed (static trace + dynamic ASAN PoC + call-site enumeration), and matches the skill's required output format (claim restatement, data-flow trace, PoC, gate review, verdict).
